front: Why does the LSTM fight vanishing gradients?
back: Additive cell update: $\partial c_t/\partial c_{t-1}$ contains $\operatorname{diag}(f_t)$ with no weight matrix and no squashing, so gradients survive when $f\approx1$.
Set $b_f$ to a positive value (1 to 5): $f\approx$ large at the start, so the cell remembers by default.
$\bar c^{tot}=\bar c_t+\bar h_t\odot o\odot(1-\tanh^2c_t)$; $\bar f=\bar c^{tot}\odot c_{t-1}$, $\bar i=\bar c^{tot}\odot g$, $\bar g=\bar c^{tot}\odot i$, $\bar c_{t-1}=\bar c^{tot}\odot f$.
$\bar a_i=\bar i\,i(1-i)$, $\bar a_f=\bar f f(1-f)$, $\bar a_g=\bar g(1-g^2)$, $\bar a_o=\bar o\,o(1-o)$; $\bar W=\bar a x^\top$, $\bar U=\bar a h_{t-1}^\top$, $\bar h_{t-1}=U^\top\bar a$.
$h_t=h_{t-1}$: the state is copied, $\partial h_t/\partial h_{t-1}\to I$ (identity path).
The candidate ignores $h_{t-1}$ and depends only on $x_t$ (start afresh).
RNN $H(n+H+1)$; GRU $3H(n+H+1)$; LSTM $4H(n+H+1)$. GRU = 3/4 of LSTM.
$4\cdot256\cdot(128+256+1)=394{,}240$ (PyTorch reports 395,264 because it has two bias vectors per gate).
Sequential computation, fixed-size state bottleneck, exploding gradients (still clip), very long (1000+) dependencies.
Cell update $c_t=f\odot c_{t-1}+\dots$ and GRU $z\odot h_{t-1}+\dots$ are learnable-gated versions of $y=x+F(x)$: an additive identity path for gradients.
